Slightly risky if stride varies but notes are thorough.

Keep Python-side forward wiring simple: branch to the optimized entrypoint only when parameter constraints match the fast path.

Avoids shared memory overhead for large windows.

For each kernel row kh, load up to 4 consecutive input elements with reinterpret_cast<float4*> when W alignment allows, else scalar fallback
Accumulate partial sums in a register float acc; divide once at end
Use __ldg() for read-only input cache hints on all global loads

strategies.intent: Warp-level reduction for small output spatial dimensions
strategies.summary: When H_out and W_out are small (e.g., global average pooling or near-global), assign one warp per output element and use warp shuffle reductions (__shfl_down_sync) to sum the pooling window elements cooperatively across lanes.

Each lane handles a subset of the kernel_size*kernel_size window elements (lane i processes elements i, i+32, i+64, ...)
After accumulation, perform warp reduction: for(int offset=16; offset>0; offset>>=1) acc += __shfl_down_sync(0xffffffff, acc, offset)

Most beneficial when kernel_size >= 8 and output is small
Can dispatch between this kernel and the tiled shared-memory kernel based on kernel_size at runtime in the C++ wrapper
strategies.expected_gain: 2-3x speedup for large pooling windows (global avg pool style) by eliminating atomic operations and using register-level communication
risk_notes: Warp divergence if kernel_size*kernel_size is not a multiple of 32; last warp iteration may have inactive lanes — mask correctly
Only beneficial for large kernel sizes; for small kernels (3x3) the overhead of warp coordination outweighs benefits

review_notes.openai-compatible: Specialized and likely low value unless the workload is near-global average pooling or very small output spatial sizes. Warp-cooperative reduction adds complexity and dispatch overhead, with limited applicability to generic AvgPool2d benchmark shapes.
review_notes.claude-compatible: Warp shuffle reduction is well-suited for large pooling windows (global avg pool style). The implementation hints are detailed and correct. However, for typical AvgPool2d benchmarks with small-to-medium kernel sizes (3x3, 5x5), this approach underperforms the tiled shared memory strategy. Conditional dispatch based on kernel_size mitigates this. Medium value, medium complexity.

strategies.intent: Persistent thread block with output channel batching
strategies.summary: Batch multiple output channels (C dimension) per thread block to improve arithmetic intensity. Each thread block processes a spatial tile for multiple channels simultaneously, reusing the thread block's shared memory across channels and reducing kernel launch overhead.
implementation_hints: Thread block processes CHANNELS_PER_BLOCK channels simultaneously; grid z-dim = ceil(N*C / CHANNELS_PER_BLOCK)
Allocate shared memory as smem[CHANNELS_PER_BLOCK][TILE_H_HALO][TILE_W_HALO]
Each thread loads one spatial position for its assigned channel; __syncthreads() before compute
Unroll the inner channel loop with #pragma unroll CHANNELS_PER_BLOCK
CHANNELS_PER_BLOCK=4 or 8 balances shared memory usage vs. reuse benefit
Particularly effective for small spatial dimensions with many channels (e.g., 512 channels, 7x7 spatial)
strategies.expected_gain: 1.5-2x improvement in memory bandwidth utilization for channel-heavy tensors by amortizing load overhead across channels
risk_notes: Shared memory per block grows as CHANNELS_PER_BLOCK * tile_area * 4 bytes; must stay under 48KB limit
If C is not divisible by CHANNELS_PER_BLOCK, add boundary guard in grid z-dim
May reduce occupancy if shared memory footprint is large; tune CHANNELS_PER_BLOCK empirically

review_notes.openai-compatible: Poor risk-adjusted fit. Cross-channel batching in shared memory offers little natural reuse for standard NCHW average pooling because channels are independent, while shared-memory pressure and occupancy risks are high. Likely overengineered for limited gain.
review_notes.claude-compatible: Channel batching per thread block can improve arithmetic intensity for channel-heavy tensors but the shared memory footprint grows quickly (CHANNELS_PER_BLOCK * tile_area * 4 bytes) and may hurt occupancy. The benefit is highly shape-dependent and the implementation complexity is high. For a general avg-pool benchmark this is likely over-engineered relative to strategies 01-02.
